statement: Define foreign exchange as FEMA, 1999 does, and describe how the foreign exchange market is organised and who takes part in it
gaps: Assessment is thin: one scored question on participants; the legal definition has only a self-assessed check.
Trading hours under FEDAI rules are not covered.
The card on the FEMA definition is held back: the Act could not be retrieved to confirm the clause and its sub-clauses.

statement: Read exchange rate quotations: direct and indirect quotes, two-way (bid and offer) quotes, and cash, tom, spot and forward value dates
Work out customer (merchant) rates, forward rates and cross rates from interbank quotes
Explain the factors that determine exchange rates and how the exchange rate mechanism works
Describe how a bank's foreign exchange dealing room operates and is controlled
gaps: RBI internal control guidelines for dealing rooms are regulation-sensitive and not yet checked against primary sources, so they are not taught.

statement: Identify the derivative products used in foreign exchange business and what each is used for
Apply the RBI and FEDAI guidelines that govern foreign exchange dealings
gaps: Drafted (Rules 1 and 6 only) but HELD BACK: FEDAI's current rulebook could not be retrieved, so applicability at the 30 June 2026 cut-off is unverified.
Rules for export, import and clean instruments, rounding and delivery (Rule 5) and RBI guidelines are not drafted; new RBI export and import regulations of January 2026 may supersede them.

statement: Explain what correspondent banking is, why banks need it, and which services depend on an account relationship
gaps: Assessment is thin: one scored question; the FATF due-diligence statements for cross-border correspondent relationships are not used.

statement: Distinguish Nostro, Vostro, Loro and mirror accounts from the direction of the relationship, and reconcile a Nostro balance
Describe the electronic modes of transmission and payment systems used for cross-border and domestic funds transfer: SWIFT, CHIPS, Fedwire, CHAPS, TARGET, RTGS and NEFT
gaps: CHAPS settlement mode: courseware (net) and Bank of England (gross) disagree; taught as a flagged caution, not scored.

statement: Identify who is an NRI or PIO under FEMA and distinguish NRE, NRO, FCNR(B) and SNRR accounts by purpose, currency, deposit form, credits, debits and repatriability
gaps: Income-tax residency tests and RFC accounts for returning NRIs are not taught (no primary source checked).
Courseware and RBI differ on the NRE term and on where rent may be credited; no item tests those points.

statement: Apply the conditions for advances against non-resident deposits and for housing loans to NRIs
gaps: One housing-loan question and one deposit-loan question each; assessment is thin for the many conditions listed.

statement: Describe the facilities available to NRIs for investing in India: shares and securities, funds, deposits, firms and immovable property
gaps: Government securities, treasury bills, PSU bonds, money-market funds and company fixed deposits are not taught (not found in the RBI sources fetched).
The new Schedule III investment limit figures (June 2026) are not stated: RBI circular 14 gives none and the Rules text was not retrieved.
Conditions on investing in a firm or proprietary concern, and the ten-year lock-in on property bought while resident, are not taught.

statement: Distinguish capital account and current account transactions and explain how the Foreign Exchange Management Act treats each
gaps: Statutory sections of FEMA (4, 6, 10(6), 11, 13) and penalties are not taught: India Code could not be checked.

statement: Apply the Liberalised Remittance Scheme: who is eligible, the annual limit, frequency, documents and how family and proprietors are treated
Identify the remittances that are permitted and those that are prohibited under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
gaps: Cash limits and foreign currency note limits for travel (courseware) are not taught: not in the Master Direction retrieved.

statement: Apply the operational conditions for capital account remittances and for gifts and loans to non-resident relatives under the scheme
gaps: Overseas direct investment procedure (forms and timelines under the 2022 Overseas Investment Rules, Regulations and Directions) is not taught: the 2022 texts were not retrieved.

statement: Work out tax collected at source on remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
gaps: The statute says 'exceeding ten lakh rupees' without stating that the rate applies to the excess only; the items compute on the excess and say so in each stem.
The additional rate where PAN or Aadhaar is missing and TCS on transfers to an NRO account are not taught.

statement: State the reporting and other remittance facilities for residents that accompany the Liberalised Remittance Scheme
gaps: The Master Direction on Reporting under FEMA (No. 18/2015-16) was not retrieved, so reporting is taught only as far as the LRS Master Direction states it (FETERS).
The courseware's daily XBRL reporting is not taught.

statement: Define a documentary letter of credit and identify each party to it and what it does
Apply the Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600) and the liabilities, responsibilities and rights of the parties
gaps: UCP 600 itself was not retrieved; articles are taught from the courseware.

statement: Distinguish the types of letter of credit: irrevocable, confirmed, transferable, red and green clause, sight, usance, deferred payment, negotiation, back-to-back, standby and revolving
Explain standby letters of credit and how they compare with guarantees
gaps: The commercial standby safeguards for imports are drafted but held back: the RBI rules behind them were not retrieved.
ISP 98 articles are not taught.

statement: Trace the flow of an export letter of credit and an import letter of credit from application to payment
gaps: The flow of an export or import credit is assessed by one question; no card walks through it step by step, and the RBI monitoring systems (EDPMS, IDPMS) are not taught.

statement: Scrutinise documents under a credit, handle discrepancies, crystallise import bills and follow up bills
gaps: Crystallisation of import bills is drafted but held back: the FEDAI guidelines it rests on could not be retrieved.
The substantive text of RBI's 16 January 2026 export-import directions (in force 1 October 2026) was not retrieved.

statement: Identify the risks in letter of credit transactions and the safeguards available to banks
Apply the Uniform Rules for Bank-to-Bank Reimbursements (URR 725)
gaps: URR 725's text was not retrieved; the 10-day and three-banking-day rules are taught as the courseware states them.

statement: Apply International Standard Banking Practice (ISBP 745) when examining documents
gaps: ISBP 745's own text was not retrieved; the courseware gives only its history and aims. The current edition is ISBP 821 (2023), which is mentioned but not taught.

statement: Apply the Incoterms 2020 rules to allocate cost, risk and delivery between buyer and seller
gaps: Incoterms 2020's rule texts were not retrieved; rule lists and allocations are taught from the trade administration page and the courseware matrix, which omits DAP.
